introduction: On this last Sunday of Advent, the readings lead us to Nazareth. King David wanted to build a house for God, but God promised to build a house for David, a kingdom that would last forever. In the Gospel, that promise is fulfilled as the angel Gabriel greets Mary and she accepts God's word. As Christmas draws near, let us ask Mary to help us make room for her Son.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: With Mary, who believed God's word, let us bring our prayers before the Father.
intentions: For the Church: that, like Mary, she may receive the Word of God with faith and bring Christ to every home. Let us pray to the Lord.
For families who are separated, poor or without a home this Christmas: that they may find welcome and care. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are struggling to believe God's promises: that they may remember that nothing spoken by God is impossible. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those travelling to be with family, and for those who will be alone: that they may be safe and know that they are loved. Let us pray to the Lord.
For our parish: that in these last days before Christmas we may make room for Christ in our hearts and our homes. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Faithful God, you kept your promise to David and gave us a Saviour born of the Virgin Mary. Hear our prayers, and make us ready to welcome him with joy. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The house God builds
reflection.body:
King David is finally at peace. He lives in a palace of cedar, while the ark of God still rests in a tent. So he decides to build God a house. It is a generous idea, and the prophet Nathan at first approves. But that night God sends Nathan back with a different message: David will not build a house for God; God will build a house for David. "Your house and your kingdom will be made sure forever before you. Your throne will be established forever."

The word "house" changes meaning in this story. David meant a building; God means a family line, a dynasty. And the promise reaches far beyond David's lifetime, to a king whose reign will have no end.

The Gospel shows us how God keeps that promise, in a way no one expected. Not in a palace in Jerusalem, but in a small village in Galilee, the angel Gabriel greets a young woman engaged to a man "of David's house." Her son will receive "the throne of his father David" and "he will reign over the house of Jacob forever."

Mary's question is honest: how can this be? The angel answers that the Holy Spirit will come upon her, and that "nothing spoken by God is impossible." Then Mary gives her consent: "Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word."

Paul calls this "the mystery which has been kept secret through long ages," now revealed. God's plans are always larger than ours. David wanted to give God a building; God wanted to give the world his Son.

In these last days before Christmas we may be busy preparing houses, meals and gifts. These are good things. But like David, we may discover that God wants to do something greater than our plans. The best preparation for Christmas is Mary's: to let God build in us, saying, "let it be done to me according to your word."
